parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires a simple HumanDriving state, an Autonomous composite with sub-states, Power On to HumanDriving, HumanDriving to Autonomous on front_distance > 10, return to HumanDriving on human steering command, brake pressed and/or when in the Auto Final sub-state, and a Power Off transition to a final state from the system. The PlantUML model implements Power On and the front_distance transition correctly and provides an Autonomous composite with AutoInitial and AutoFinal. Non-conformances are in the handling of Power Off and in how the return to HumanDriving and the final state are modeled.

issues.issue: Power Off transition is only defined from HumanDriving
issues.reason: Specification 5 says when power off it will transit to final state. The model only allows Power Off from HumanDriving; there is no Power Off transition defined for the Autonomous composite/sub-states, so a power off while in Autonomous cannot reach the final state.
issues.where: HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off and missing transition from Autonomous

issues.issue: Power Off target is the terminator [*] instead of an explicit final state
issues.reason: Specification 5 requires a transition to a final state on power off. The model terminates to [*], i.e., the UML final/terminator node, and does not model a named final state as implied by the specification.

issues.issue: Return to HumanDriving is modeled as a composite-level exit with guard in(AutoFinal) instead of a sub-state transition
issues.reason: Specification 4 requires transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final). The model places the transition on the Autonomous composite with a guard 'in (AutoFinal)'. This allows human_steering_cmd and brake_pressed to exit Autonomous from AutoInitial as well, and it uses 'in (AutoFinal)' as a guard rather than modeling the return as originating from the AutoFinal sub-state. The intended semantics is a transition from the AutoFinal sub-state / when the system is in AutoFinal, not a composite guard.

issues.issue: Transition from Autonomous to HumanDriving is enabled by the guard in(AutoFinal) alone
issues.reason: With the OR guard, the model will immediately take the return transition whenever the current sub-state is AutoFinal, regardless of an explicit event. The specification describes a transition triggered by human steering cmd, brake pressed, or being in auto final, not an unconditional exit as soon as AutoFinal is entered.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
